node.label: Millions place
node.description: Interpret millions and related places in large whole numbers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ten hundreds make one thousand
node.description: A group of ten hundreds can be treated as one thousand.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Periods group three digits
node.description: Large numbers are read in three-digit periods such as ones, thousands and millions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Large places show magnitude
node.description: The leftmost nonzero place usually gives the main scale of a whole number.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expanded form preserves value
node.description: Expanded form shows the same number as a sum of place values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Left place is ten times right place
node.description: Each place to the left is worth ten times the place to its right.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rounding uses a target place
node.description: A rounded number keeps the requested place and adjusts lower places.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rounding uses closest benchmark
node.description: Rounding chooses the nearest benchmark for the requested place value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Estimation uses approximation
node.description: An estimate is close enough for a purpose but is not necessarily exact.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compatible numbers are easier to compute
node.description: Compatible numbers make mental calculation or estimation easier while staying near the original values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reasonableness uses magnitude
node.description: A reasonable answer fits the size expected from the numbers and operation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Commas change value
node.description: Learner thinks commas create the value rather than helping group digits for reading.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: More digits always larger in any context
node.description: Learner applies whole-number digit-count comparison even when context later involves decimals or other notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rounding always increases
node.description: Learner believes rounding always makes a number larger.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Estimate is exact answer
node.description: Learner treats an estimate as if it must equal the exact answer.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Round all digits independently
node.description: Learner changes several digits independently instead of rounding to a target place.

edge.rationale: Large whole-number work includes extending place value to thousands.
Large whole-number work includes interpreting ten-thousands and hundred-thousands places.
Millions extend the same place-value period structure to larger numbers.
Reading and writing large numbers practises grouping digits into periods.
Reading and writing large whole numbers is a central large-number task.
Large-number expanded form makes each place value explicit.
Comparing and ordering large numbers uses place-value magnitude.
Scaled number lines are a useful representation for large-number magnitude.
Powers-of-ten scaling generalises whole-number place value.
Rounding to tens and hundreds is an early core rounding task.
Rounding to thousands extends rounding to larger place values.
Number lines support deciding which benchmark is nearest.
Halfway cases are a focused part of rounding conventions and reasoning.
Estimating sums and differences commonly uses rounded numbers.
Compatible numbers are a related estimation strategy using friendly nearby values.
Reasonableness checking practises estimation and magnitude judgement.
Thousands extend the hundreds-tens-ones place-value structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain one thousand as ten hundreds or as a new place-value unit.

edge.rationale: Ten-thousands and hundred-thousands extend the thousands place-value unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads larger places as isolated digits instead of grouped place values.

edge.rationale: Millions extend the place-value structure beyond thousands and hundred-thousands.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot group or name places beyond hundred-thousands.

edge.rationale: Place-value periods build on recognising thousands as a named group of places.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads every digit separately rather than by three-digit periods.

edge.rationale: Reading and writing large numbers depends on grouping digits into periods.
edge.failure_signal: Learner misreads or miswrites large numbers with omitted period names or misplaced digits.

edge.rationale: Expanded form for large numbers depends on identifying each digit's place value in notation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expands digits as single values rather than place values.

edge.rationale: Comparing large numbers requires reading their places and magnitude accurately.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares later digits before considering the largest differing place.

edge.rationale: Locating large numbers on a scaled line depends on ordering and approximate magnitude.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places numbers evenly without considering scale intervals.

edge.rationale: Powers-of-ten scaling generalises patterns across larger whole-number places.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain each place as ten times the place to its right.

edge.rationale: Rounding to tens and hundreds depends on understanding those places in whole numbers.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes digits without identifying the target place.

edge.rationale: Number-line rounding depends on comparing distances or order around benchmarks.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot tell which benchmark a number is closer to on a number line.

edge.rationale: Halfway cases depend on recognising equal distance between two benchmarks.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats midpoint cases inconsistently or as always closer to the lower benchmark.

edge.rationale: Rounding to thousands requires interpreting thousands and neighbouring places.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the thousands place or the digit used to decide the rounding direction.

edge.rationale: Estimating sums and differences often uses rounded addends or minuends.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot choose rounded numbers before estimating a calculation.

edge.rationale: Compatible-number estimation extends rounding-based estimation to friendlier nearby values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses numbers that are easy but not close enough for a useful estimate.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checks depend on estimating expected magnitude before or after calculation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts an answer that is far outside a plausible estimated range.
